description: A PHP static analysis tool for finding errors and security vulnerabilities in PHP applications

latest_release.body:
<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at 4303c7dbbc23efaac3d988707b4acf4d5508a9cc -->

## What's Changed
### Features
* Make allowStringToStandInForClass consistent across class-string usages by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13702
* Add `Codebase::addReportableFiles()` to report issues in files Psalm doesn't analyze by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13725
* Narrow array_filter() results with first-class callable callbacks by @kamil-tekiela in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12524
* Narrow a string to empty or non-empty from strlen() compared with 0 or 1 by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12597
* Report a float that loses its fraction as an operand of a bitwise or modulo operation by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/12623
### Fixes
* fix(algebra): an operand of an || that can never be true is paradoxical by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13689
* fix(reconciler): a lowercase or literal string can be asserted to be the name of a class or a callable by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13685
* fix(reconciler): !is_iterable() drops the objects that are Traversable by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13686
* Fix false positive null array access diagnostics in unset() by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13663
* Fix dynamic method call reachability in unused code analysis by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13668
* fix(algebra): a not-null check after isset() of the same variable is redundant by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13692
* fix(scope): a switch default that falls through without returning does not end the function by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13684
* fix(unused): a read in a try body after an assignment does not use the values the assignment overwrote by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13704
* fix(reconciler): array_key_exists() of a string in an array of int keys narrows it to the keys as strings by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13690
* fix(properties): a class extending a universal object crate keeps the properties it declares by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13703
* fix(reconciler): a negated isset of a possibly undefined variable is null by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13706
* Fix `@mixin` lookup order: own, traits, parents; first declared wins by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13694
* Print exact types in argument, return type and signature mismatch messages by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13717
* Fix crash when Psalm is used as a library without a check method (nullable `$project_files`) by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13719
* Fix stubs that redeclare properties of builtin or already stubbed classes by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13720
* Don't report an || operand reading a variable the condition assigns by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13724
* Fix overly broad invalidation of memoized getters after unrelated object mutations by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13662
* fix(context): a block that forgot a variable leaves its type as it was before the block by @jirkace in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13705
* Fix: an inaccessible method hides the mixin method reached through `__call()` by @alies-dev in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13727
* Keep the key and value types of a negated iterable assertion on Traversable by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13732
* Treat the bound of a template a receiver leaves out as a stand-in by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13733
* Resolve static::$p to its property when it is passed by reference by @orklah in https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/pull/13730
* Report a stringable object in the index column of array_column since PHP 8 by @orklah in https://gith

detail.readme:
Psalm

[![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/dt/vimeo/psalm.svg)](https://packagist.org/packages/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm coverage](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/coverage.svg?)](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm) [![Psalm level](https://shepherd.dev/github/vimeo/psalm/level.svg?)](https://psalm.dev/) Psalm is a static analysis tool for finding errors in PHP applications. [Join the official Psalm news channel](https://t.me/psalmphp) and the Psalm community on [Telegram](https://t.me/psalmphp_community) and [Discord](https://discord.gg/RwH8rEpxt9)! ## Installation To get started, check out the [installation guide](docs/running_psalm/installation.md). ## Live Demo You can play around with Psalm [on its website](https://psalm.dev/). ## Documentation Documentation is available on [Psalm’s website](https://psalm.dev/docs), generated from the [docs](https://github.com/vimeo/psalm/blob/master/docs) folder. ## Support Psalm development You can support Psalm development by requesting a support contract from [Daniil Gentili](https://daniil.it), the only active maintainer of Psalm. Support contracts can cover full integration of Psalm into existing codebases, support for Psalm issues and development of additional Psalm features. See [here »](https://daniil.it) for info, pricing and contact information. ## Interested in contributing? Have a look at [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Who made this Built by Matt Brown ([@muglug](https://github.com/muglug)). Maintained by Daniil Gentili ([@danog](https://github.com/danog)), Alies Lapatsin ([@alies-dev](https://github.com/alies-dev)) and Orklah ([@orklah](https://github.com/orklah)). Former maintainer: Bruce Weirdan ([@weirdan](https://github.com/weirdan)). The engineering team at [Vimeo](https://github.com/vimeo) have provided a lot encouragement, especially [@nbeliard](https://github.com/nbeliard), [@erunion](https://github.com/erunion) and [@nickyr](https://github.com/nickyr).
